To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inoculation of sorghum seedings with nitrogen-fixingbacteria increases the amount of14C-compound exudation from the roots.
the inoculation of sorghum with nitrogen-fixing microorganisms increases root exudation.

(1) the amount of organic carbon exuded from the roots is increased when the plants are inoculated with nitrogen fixing bacteria; (2) the increase in exudation is proportional to the amount of mineral nitrogen supplied and to the growth of the bacteria; and (3) the increase in organic exudation occurs when the bacteria are supplied with carbon but not with nitrogen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of inoculation of sorghum plants with nitrogen-fixing micro-organisms on the exudation of organic components by sorghum roots.
the effects of nitrogen-fixing bacteria on the exudation of organic compounds from roots of sorghum.
the effects of inoculation of sorghum seedling roots with nitrogen-fixing and non nitrogen-fixing bacteria on root exudation, plant growth, and nitrogen nutrition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the increased amounts of14C in root exudates from inoculated plants were due to increased growth of the bacteria, and that this increased growth was due to increased availability of mineral nitrogen to the plants.

nitrogen-fixing bacteria, when present in the rhizosphere, may increase the amounts of organic compounds released into the soil solution, and thus may increase the amount of organic carbon available to microorganisms in the rhizospehere.
the increased root exudation observed in the present study was not due to increased bacterial growth, but was probably due to a direct effect of the bacteria on the plant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
root exudation is increased by inoculation with nitrogen fixing bacteria and that this effect is dependent upon the presence of mineral nitrogen in the medium.
the root exudates of sorghum are altered in composition and amount by the presence of nitrogen-fixing bacteria, and that this alteration is related to the nitrogen status of the plants.
nitrogen-fixing bacteria can increase the amount of root exudate by sorghum plants, and the increased root exudate can be utilized by the bacteria for nitrogen fixation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
root exudation is a significant component of plant nutrition and that nitrogen-fixing bacteria can increase root exudation.
root exudates are important for the growth and development of plants.
root exudates of sorghum are affected by nitrogen-fixing bacteria, and that the effects are dependent on the nitrogen supply to the plant.
